Abstract This paper explores the impact of consumer behavior and product design on the willingness to repurchase tea sets. As the Chinese economic model increasingly relies on consumption, tea sets are receiving increasing attention as a hot selling category. Against the backdrop of the Asia–Pacific region dominating global sales, especially in the Chinese market, the tea market has maintained a stable annual growth rate, making it particularly important to understand consumers' willingness to repurchase. Although previous studies have explored the application of consumer satisfaction and loyalty in various fields, relatively little specialized research has been conducted on the tea market. The analysis focuses on teapot design and its relationship with consumer demand. It emphasizes improving economic benefits through innovative product design, rather than functional improvements, by integrating factors such as price perception, service quality, and physical display. This paper examines how consumer behavior and product design affect the repurchase intentions of tea sets. As the Chinese economy becomes more consumption-driven, tea sets are gaining popularity as a hot-selling category. With the Asia–Pacific region, particularly China, dominating global sales, the tea market has consistently grown annually, highlighting the need to understand consumer repurchase intentions. Although previous studies have investigated consumer satisfaction and loyalty across different sectors, research specific to the tea market remains limited. This study focuses on the relationship between teapot design and consumer demand. The study emphasizes enhancing economic benefits through innovative product design rather than merely functional improvements, considering factors such as price perception, service quality, and physical display. This study fills a gap in the literature and explores the impact of design novelty and pattern aesthetics on purchase intentions. The results of this study can guide enterprises in enhancing their competitiveness in the tea market by aligning design with consumer preferences. Consumers can make wise choices and potentially increase economic returns by understanding the factors influencing purchasing decisions. The research results provide a new perspective on how tea set design can promote consumer repurchase intention, which is an area that has not been deeply explored in the current literature. Keywords: consumer behavior, market competitiveness, product design, repurchase intention, tea set 1. Repurchase intention (RI) has been extensively explored in both academic and practical fields over the past few decades (Hansen, 2013). However, few studies have focused on how teapot design impacts consumer repurchase intentions. Teware, as a tangible product catering to personalized consumer needs, warrants further exploration. Research has identified gaps in product design, development, and marketing. However, these studies have overlooked the interaction between products and consumers, especially the factors affecting consumers' willingness to buy teapots. This study aims to address this gap by investigating the relationship between customer needs and teapot design. The focus is on two key aspects, shape design and pattern design, both of which significantly influence consumers' purchase intentions (Zainal Abidin et al., 2008). Companies generate consumer interest through two main approaches in new product development: first, by meeting consumer needs through new functionalities, and second, by shaping purchase intentions through product design (Hassan et al., 2022). With many products offering similar functions, achieving breakthroughs in innovation has become costly and challenging. In contrast, product design can significantly increase the survival rate of high-tech products (Hasan et al., 2023). Consequently, companies are prioritizing the economic advantages of product design and implementing design innovation strategies to achieve sustainable competitive advantages. The study also investigates the roles of price perception, service quality, and tangible display, which reflect fundamental consumer needs. Designers face challenges due to the growing diversity in consumers' teaware preferences. However, both designers and brands often lack a clear understanding of consumer preferences, creating challenges for teapot products in both online and offline markets. Teapot design continues to evolve to attract consumers and address their needs. This study focuses on how the shape and pattern designs of teapots affect consumer repurchase intentions. It also investigates the mediating roles of cognitive positivity and emotional response in this process and examines how brand credibility moderates this influence. To address these questions, we developed a comprehensive mechanism model that integrates the mediating and moderating factors discussed above. From a practical perspective, the study’s insights can guide businesses in prioritizing teaware design, enhancing product competitiveness and driving economic benefits. Consumers may also make more informed decisions aligned with their preferences. Theoretically, this study is the first to link tea ware product design with consumers repurchase intentions, filling a gap in the literature (Li & Li, 2022). By incorporating cognitive positivity, emotional response, and brand credibility, this research enriches the fields of consumer behavior and product design. 2. Theoretical background 2.1. Concept of repurchase intention https://www.malque.pub/ojs/index.php/msj Lin and Abidin (2026) 3 Delias et al. (2022) defined repurchase intention as the likelihood of a consumer purchasing a product or service before repeatedly using it in the future and suggested that maintaining customer repurchase intention plays a very important role. Zhang et al. (2020) suggested that customer satisfaction is very important for customer purchasing behavior. Cultural consumption, such as enriching knowledge, artistic and cultural influence, and motivation for physical and mental pleasure, is also an important factor affecting consumers' willingness to purchase tea sets. The humanistic spirit contained in tea culture has a significant effect on consumers' psychology (such as healthy lifestyle motivation, visual effect satisfaction motivation, etc.), which can effectively promote the improvement of their consumption willingness and thus enhance their repurchase intention (Leonce et al., 2019). Wang et al. (2021) proposed that purchase intention is an attitude toward whether to make a purchase on the basis of a comprehensive evaluation of product information and self-information. Zhang et al. (2020) noted that purchase intention is the tendency of consumers to purchase a certain product or service, that is, the probability of engaging in purchasing behavior. According to Zhang et al. (2023), there is intention first, followed by action. The stronger the purchase intention is, the greater the likelihood of making a purchase. Purchasing behavior occurs after purchase intention, which can predict repurchase intention. Similarly, Valeri et al. (2024) reported that purchase intentions, to some extent, represent consumers' attitudes and the likelihood of purchasing a certain product in the future and can predict consumers’ repurchase intentions. 2.2. Theories of emotions The states of affectivity have long been established to have an interdependent relationship with the logical reasoning process. In the feelings-as-information paradigm, the current affective state serves as a prominent information source, which can influence the judgment of consumers (Minton et al., 2023). Emotion is an effective tool for measuring the degree of emotional activation, which affects an individual's cognitive process and thus affects consumer behavior. Jennifer et al. (2003) argued that immediate emotions have a direct effect on an individual's immediate decision-making or behavior and an indirect effect on their expected outcomes and behavioral decision-making expectations. The exchange and interaction of information between people and products can generate different emotional experiences: the primary task of a product is not just to achieve functionality or serve consumers' lives but also to satisfy emotions; affective reactions must be evaluated along with cognitive reactions because both reactions serve as pivotal inputs in decision-making under a symbiotic relationship, although affective reactions play a more dominant role, as emotions can pervert perceptions and beliefs (Palomba et al., 2021). Affective reactions are the foundation of emotions, motivation, information processing, and behavioral reactions. External stimuli cause changes in consumers' emotional states, leading to positive or negative aesthetic evaluations of the product, which in turn affect their repurchase intention. For product design, consumers will feel excited due to the high level of novelty in the design (Mohamed Kamil et al., 2018). The greater the potential for emotional arousal is, the greater the level of affective reactions experienced (Semerikov et al., 2021), and affective reactions affect the aesthetic evaluation of product design. Therefore, this study evaluated both affective and cognitive reactions to reflect the symbiotic cycle that exists in real-life decision-making. 3. Hypotheses 3.1. Customer satisfaction The concept of customer satisfaction has been defined by many scholars. After purchasing, the customer will have an overall perceived evaluation of the entire purchasing process, process, and outcome (Nimran et al., 2020). It is also based on affective reactions; Simonas (2022) proposed that consumers' shopping behavior is intended to fulfill their needs. After shopping, consumers evaluate whether their needs have been fulfilled and to what extent they have been met, which generates psychological reactions. Yusriadi et al. (2023) reported that there is a positive correlation between customer satisfaction and customer loyalty. Satisfaction is the cumulative evaluation of all consumer experiences, whereas loyalty is the expectation or tendency of customers to repeat purchases of a specific product or service (Cezar et al., 2020). Furthermore, Wang et al. (2023) studied the factors that affect online store satisfaction and repurchase intentions. Research has shown that customer perception and online store experience play significant roles. High customer satisfaction can promote customer repurchase. Hence, the following hypothesis is constructed. H1: Customer satisfaction positively correlates with repurchase intention. 3.2. Brand credibility Researchers have claimed that celebrities make advertisements more credible (Fatma et al., 2023). Accordingly, according to the meaning transfer model (Abidin et al., 2020), celebrities are expected to transfer meanings such as reputation, personality, and values to their brand or product through endorsement. Research has shown that brand credibility has a positive effect on customers' purchasing behavior. In addition, emotions can also have a significant effect on product information processing. Brand credibility inference refers to the perceived credibility of product information embedded in a brand. A trustworthy brand is associated with higher perceived quality, lower perceived risk, and lower information cost, leading to higher expected utility and consideration formation (Garcia et al., 2024). As is well known, brand reputation can lead https://www.malque.pub/ojs/index.php/msj Lin and Abidin (2026) 4 to favorable marketing results, such as loyalty and purchase intentions. On the basis of the theoretical arguments and empirical evidence, brand credibility is, therefore, included in the research framework as a moderator, with the hypotheses formulated as follows. H2a: Brand credibility moderates the relationship between affective reactions and customer satisfaction. H2b: Brand credibility moderates the relationship between customer satisfaction and repurchase intention. 3.3. Affective reactions Affective reactions (AR) can be defined by the pleasure, arousal, and dominance (PAD) dimensions of affective reactions to external environmental encounters; however, the PAD typology was proposed by Peterson et al. (2020). They reported that pleasure and arousal can encompass all the emotional states of an individual. However, Liu et al. (2021) argued that the PAD typology is too narrow to encompass the comprehensiveness of AR. Therefore, other emotions and feelings (such as affection and intimacy) should also be examined (Forth et al., 2022). Previous studies have shown that visual stimuli presented through product design novelty can alter consumers' emotions, thereby influencing their decision-making. In addition, the satisfaction, product emotion, and personal intimacy that customers experience while shopping all contribute to improving customer satisfaction (Abidin et al., 2017). This is because shoppers may exhibit proximity behavior while pleasantly shopping (Youngstrom et al., 2024). Hence, the following hypothesis is formulated: H3: Affective reactions positively correlate with customer satisfaction. 3.4. Cognitive reactions Cognitive reactions (CRs) refer to mental processes triggered by an encounter with a stimulus (Fiorio et al., 2021). Customers pay attention to the functionality, experience, cost, and time savings of goods or services and conduct cognitive evaluations that are beneficial to themselves, others, and the external environment. CR acts as the basis for AR, whereby information must be deemed reliable before emotional attachment to wards, individuals, brands, or products can be established (Wang et al., 2021). For some high-value products or services, consumers often pay more attention to the unique experience and enjoyment they bring, and these unique cognitive reactions can affect customers' purchasing decisions and consumption behavior (Czarneca et al., 2024). Hence, the following hypothesis is formulated: H4: Cognitive reactions positively correlate with affective reactions. 3.5. Price perception Price perception (PP) is defined as the perceived monetary value of a product or service. Price has always been an important driving factor for purchase intentions, as monetary factors when products and services are purchased can affect overall perceived value (Gusti et al., 2020). The price factor directly affects consumers' perception of benefits, and consumers' price sensitivity to products or services is often closely related to the perceived benefits they can bring. If consumers perceive that a product or service can bring greater benefits, their sensitivity to price tends to be lower (Ardiansyah et al., 2021). For example, consumers are often more willing to pay higher prices for goods or services that can bring happiness, enjoyment, value, quality, and other benefits. Promotions and other factors are also closely related to customers' price perceptions. In promotions, sellers can attract consumers by promoting information such as product benefits or discounts, which can enhance consumers' cognitive reactions to the product. In addition, consumers can experience different atmospheres and service experiences in specific places, and the atmosphere, service experience, and personal habits of such places can also affect consumers' cognitive reactions and purchasing decisions (Abidin et al., 2014). Hence, the following hypothesis is constructed. H5: Price perception positively correlates with cognitive reactions. 3.6. Physical evidence Physical evidence refers to all tangible components that can convey service characteristics and advantages within the scope of service marketing management (Sree, et al., 2020). Salespeople can provide services to consumers through presentation forms such as text, color, sound, video, images, and physical displays, thereby generating perceptions (Rawat et al., 2021). Physical evidence is a way for consumers to further understand tea set products. Previous studies have suggested that product design reflects regional visual symbols, combining cultural customs, aesthetic characteristics, ethnic culture, and various materials, spirits, and behaviors in social culture, which can effectively arouse consumer recognition (Suganda et al., 2022). During the purchasing process, the display of products by merchants significantly positively influences consumers' affective reactions. Consumers can enhance their artistic perception of products or services through the characteristics and value of the products displayed by merchants. The information displayed by a product (such as color, shape, packaging, etc.) can affect consumers' judgment of the product, which in turn affects their purchase intention for the product. Hence, the following hypotheses are constructed. H6: Physical evidence positively correlates with cognitive reactions. H7: Physical evidence positively correlates with affective reactions. https://www.malque.pub/ojs/index.php/msj Lin and Abidin (2026) 5 3.7. Service quality Nabella et al. (2023) proposed that service quality refers to the sum of the process and results of a service product being delivered to customers in a certain service environment. Service quality includes three aspects: the product, delivery, and environment of the service. The impact of a company's service quality is multifaceted and involves individual emotions, perceptions, and communication between the company's providers, according to Ali et al. (2021). Moreover, Hameed et al. (2022) argued that the affective reactions of customers to service quality run through the entire customer consumption experience, including psychological expectations before consumption, actual experiences during consumption, and comparisons between perceived results after consumption and psychological expectations before consumption. Alibazoglu et al. (2020) suggested that the higher the quality of service is, the more evident its own value will be, which will further improve consumer satisfaction. Endeshaw (2021) reported that service quality has a positive effect on trust and perceived value in Malaysia's service industries (banking, insurance, and telecommunications). Yusuf et al. (2023) investigated the impact of service quality and identified the influence of satisfaction on word-of-mouth and repurchase intention. Hence, the following hypotheses are constructed. H8: Service quality positively correlates with cognitive reactions. H9: Service quality positively correlates with affective reactions. 3.8. Modeling design The visual stimulation brought by product design is the most convenient way to attract consumers' attention (Abidin et al., 2008), and it is also an excellent opportunity to gain a differentiated competitive advantage in the market (Abidin et al., 2023). Therefore, many companies have begun to use product design as a competitive tool, viewing it as a way to highlight new products in saturated product markets, produce more innovative products, and achieve commercial success (Toyong et al., 2021). Research has shown that in the design of teapots, essential requirements must be met first. This is what ceramic tea set users believe teapot products must meet, such as a comfortable grip of the tea handle. Second, there is a demand for a desirable shape, such as smooth water flow from the spout, which is an important factor in product experience and quality competition. Finally, there is an exciting demand that can provide users and buyers with new visual and emotional experiences, resonate, achieve product differentiation, and enhance competitiveness (Timoshenko et al., 2023). Thus, the hypothesis is formulated as follows. H10: A modeling design positively correlates with affective reactions. 3.9. Pattern design The design of teapot patterns is also important because of the different preferences of customers. Designers attempt to convey product information to elicit strong reactions from consumers by changing factors such as form, material, and color in teapot design (Li and Li, 2022). When new products enter the market, consumers first notice the visual information presented by the product design. First, innovative product design attracts consumers to learn more about the product and increases the probability of purchase; second, consumers may also increase their interest and purchase probability due to traditional cultural factors in product design (Maria et al., 2018). Hence, the following hypothesis is constructed. H11: Pattern design positively correlates with affective experience. 3.10. Model path analysis 4.5.1. Structural equation modeling path analysis First, as shown in Table 7, this study focuses on the path estimation values and their statistical significance, which indicate the degree and direction of direct influence between each variable. From the estimated path values, cognitive reactions have a significant positive effect on price perception and service quality (estimated values of 0.277 and 0.330, respectively), indicating that these two variables have an important positive relationship in the model. In contrast, the impact of cognitive reactions on physical evidence is not significant (estimated value of 0.005, P value of 0.942), indicating that there is no statistically significant direct relationship between them. Second, standardized regression weights show the contribution of each variable to the target variable while controlling for the influence of other variables. The standardized regression weight of affective reactions for cognitive reactions is 0.357, which means that affective reactions have a stronger explanatory power for cognitive reactions under the influence of other variables. This analysis not only helps us understand the individual contributions of each variable but also reveals their mechanisms of action in the overall model. The overall analysis of the model revealed that affective reactions play an important role in connecting other variables in the model. This finding indicates that although the direct impact of affective reactions and brand credibility on customer satisfaction is not significant, there may be important interactions between them. Further analysis shows that brand credibility has a moderating effect on the relationship between affective reactions and customer satisfaction at different levels. For example, when the brand reputation value is 2.25, the effect of affective reactions on customer satisfaction is 0.0748, but the p value is 0.3124, which is not significant; however, when the brand reputation value is 4, this effect significantly increases to 0.3295 (p<. 001), indicating that high brand reputation can enhance the positive impact of affective reactions on customer satisfaction. In summary, brand reputation does play a moderating role between affective reactions and customer satisfaction, especially when brand reputation is high, and it can significantly enhance the impact of affective reactions on customer satisfaction. This discovery not only helps to deepen the understanding of the mechanisms behind consumer behavior but also suggests that brand managers need to pay attention to the combined effects of affective reactions and brand reputation in improving customer satisfaction. 5. Discussion This study empirically investigates how teapot design influences consumers repurchase intentions. The results presented in Figure 4 and Table 10 support most of the proposed hypotheses. These findings align with the theoretical framework, confirming the expected relationship between consumer behavior and product design. Customer satisfaction shows a significant positive correlation with repurchase intentions, confirming that satisfaction serves as a core driver of repurchase, which is consistent with existing theories. Emotional response significantly enhances customer satisfaction, suggesting that consumers' emotional states directly affect their satisfaction with products or services, underscoring the role https://www.malque.pub/ojs/index.php/msj Lin and Abidin (2026) 11 of emotions in consumer behavior. The cognitive response positively affects the emotional response, implying that cognitive processes shape emotional experiences, which subsequently influence purchasing behavior. Both price perception and service quality positively affect cognitive response, highlighting their importance in shaping consumers' cognitive evaluations. Reasonable prices and high-quality service enhance cognitive appraisals, further influencing purchase decisions. Tangible display, however, does not significantly affect cognitive response, possibly because consumers prioritize functionality and design over tangible display when purchasing teapots. Nevertheless, tangible display, shape design, and pattern design positively affect emotional response, demonstrating that visual design elements evoke emotional resonance in consumers. Attractive shape and pattern designs enhance aesthetic experiences and reinforce emotional connections with the product. Service quality does not significantly affect emotional response, suggesting that for culturally and aesthetically significant products such as teapots, emotional experiences are driven more by design and cultural meaning than by service quality. Brand credibility significantly moderates the relationship between emotional response and customer satisfaction, indicating that high brand credibility amplifies the effect of emotional response on satisfaction. Consumers with high brand trust are more likely to translate positive emotions into greater satisfaction. However, brand credibility does not significantly moderate the link between customer satisfaction and repurchase intentions, possibly because customer satisfaction directly influences repurchase intentions more prominently, with the moderating effect of brand credibility being relatively weaker in the teapot market. This finding indicates that reasonable pricing and high-quality service strongly enhance consumers' cognitive evaluations (Natalia et al., 2023). Second, cognitive response significantly influences emotional response. The path coefficient for this relationship is 0.36 (p < 0.001). This suggests that positive cognitive evaluations lead to positive emotional experiences, aligning with the theoretical model's hypothesis of interaction between cognition and emotion. Among the factors influencing emotional response, the path coefficients for tangible display, shape design, and pattern design are 0.31, 0.14, and 0.16, respectively. All p values are significant, indicating that these design elements positively influence emotional response. The strongest impact comes from tangible displays, suggesting that businesses should emphasize product presentation to evoke emotional resonance among consumers (Dandis et al., 2021). The influence of service quality on emotional response is not statistically significant. The path coefficient is 0.02, with a nonsignificant p value. This suggests that for products with strong aesthetic and cultural value, such as teaware, consumers' emotional experiences primarily stem from the product's design and https://www.malque.pub/ojs/index.php/msj Lin and Abidin (2026) 12 cultural content. The path coefficient for the effect of emotional response on customer satisfaction is 0.34 (p < 0.001), indicating that emotional experience significantly positively impacts customer satisfaction and confirming the role of emotion in customer satisfaction (Veloso & Sousa, 2021). The path coefficient for customer satisfaction on repurchase intention is 0.29 (p < 0.001), reinforcing that satisfaction is a crucial factor influencing repurchase behavior (Afriani & Setyono, 2020). Brand credibility significantly moderates the relationship between emotional response and customer satisfaction. However, it does not significantly moderate the relationship between customer satisfaction and repurchase intention. This finding indicates that brand credibility enhances the influence of emotional experience on satisfaction. In driving repurchase, however, the direct impact of satisfaction is more pronounced. These results are consistent with the theoretical model and validate the interactions among cognition, emotion, and satisfaction in consumer behavior. For practical implications, businesses should prioritize pricing strategies and service quality to improve consumers' cognitive evaluations. They should also enhance product design and presentation to evoke emotional resonance and improve satisfaction and repurchase intentions. Brand building remains crucial, particularly in enhancing the influence of emotional experience on satisfaction. However, to promote repurchase, businesses should prioritize enhancing customer satisfaction itself. Figure 4 Assuming path coefficients. From a broader perspective, the results support the model's overall feasibility. The findings emphasize the key roles of product design, price perception, and service quality in influencing consumers repurchase intentions. However, the unsupported hypotheses offer valuable insights for business innovation and development. First, the insignificant effect of tangible displays on cognitive response may indicate that in the digital era, consumers prefer to gather product information online rather than relying on physical displays. This suggests that businesses should enhance their digital marketing strategies. They should optimize online product presentation and the user experience to meet consumer needs (Saraswati & Indriani, 2021). Second, the insignificant effect of service quality on emotional response indicates that for culturally significant products, such as teaware, consumers' emotional experiences are derived primarily from cultural content and design aesthetics rather than the service process (Frooghi et al., 2022). Therefore, businesses should focus on highlighting the cultural value of their products. They should integrate traditional elements with modern design to craft unique brand stories that enhance emotional resonance with consumers. Additionally, the lack of significant moderation by brand credibility between customer satisfaction and repurchase intention suggests that, in the teaware market, customer satisfaction directly influences repurchase intention more prominently. The brand's moderating effect is relatively limited (Patel et al., 2023). This finding indicates that businesses should focus not only on improving product quality and customer satisfaction but also on directly encouraging repurchase behavior. This can be accomplished through membership programs, personalized recommendations, and value-added services. However, this study has several limitations. The data collection was restricted to specific regions and groups, potentially affecting the generalizability of the results. Future research should broaden the sample scope to include consumers from various regions and cultural backgrounds. Furthermore, this study focuses exclusively on the teaware market. Other product categories may demonstrate different consumer behavior patterns. Testing the model’s applicability in other industries is recommended. Finally, as market environments and consumer preferences evolve, future research should examine the impact of emerging technologies and trends on consumer behavior. Technologies such as artificial intelligence and virtual reality can enhance consumer experiences and should be included in future studies. Theoretical implications This research explores the impact of tea set product design on consumer repurchase intentions from several aspects. First, affective factors play an important role in the formation of consumers' intentions to repurchase. Consumers' aesthetic enjoyment of product design, emotional identification with traditional cultural values, and emotional connection with the brand have all been proven to be important factors in determining consumer decisions, according to Hussain et al. (2021). Second, cognitive factors also have a profound effect on consumers' intention to repurchase. Consumers' cognitive evaluation of product quality, brand reputation, and user experience directly affects their decision-making process and brand loyalty (Gao et al. (2023)). Further research indicates that cultural factors also play an important role in consumer purchasing behavior. The respect for and recognition of tea culture traditions by consumers, as well as the influence of individual cultural backgrounds on purchasing behavior, cannot be ignored in influencing the formation of repurchase intentions (Yang et al., 2020). Finally, changes in market competition and environmental factors have also had a significant effect on consumers' intentions to repurchase. The rise of emerging brands and intensified market competition have led consumers to pay more attention to the differentiated features of products and the market competitiveness of brands when choosing tea sets. Abidin et al. (2024). Therefore, the formation of consumers' intentions to repurchase tea sets is influenced not only by affective, cognitive, and cultural factors but also by market competition and environmental changes. 6.2. Practical implications The results generated from this research provide some insightful practical implications for enhancing consumers' intention to repurchase tea sets in actual marketing and product design. First, the importance of emotional factors indicates that consumers' emotional connection and identification with products play crucial roles in determining their intention to repurchase. By designing tea set products that can evoke emotional resonance and cultural identity among consumers, their loyalty to the brand and their intention to repurchase can be effectively enhanced. Second, the influence of cognitive factors shows that consumers' cognitive evaluations of product quality, brand reputation, and user experience directly affect their repurchase decisions. Therefore, enhancing brand reputation and cognitive evaluation through effective brand management strategies can promote the formation of consumers' intentions to repurchase (Mithun et al., 2023). Moreover, regularly adjusting product positioning, brand strategies, and marketing activities to adapt to market changes and competitive pressures is one of the key strategies used to increase consumers' intention to repurchase. Through market monitoring and consumer feedback analysis, companies can capture changes in consumer demand in a timely manner and develop more attractive and effective marketing strategies, thereby enhancing product market competitiveness and consumer brand loyalty (Safitri et al., 2024). This not only helps to enhance the market competitiveness of the product and consumers' intention to repurchase but also promotes the long-term development and success of the brand. 7. Conclusions Given the increasing popularity of Chinese tea culture, brands and retailers must recognize the changing trends in consumer shopping journeys to seize this opportunity. This research proposes a comprehensive framework that elucidates how consumers' intention to repurchase is influenced by multiple factors, including emotional, cognitive, and cultural factors, and ultimately translates into repurchase intention and behavior. This research further emphasizes that the influence of cultural factors is reflected in consumers' acceptance of cultural elements and traditions integrated into product design. In summary, through in-depth analysis of consumer behavior and market trends, this research enables businesses to develop effective marketing strategies and product design concepts, thereby enhancing consumer purchasing decisions and brand loyalty. This not only helps to enhance the market competitiveness of enterprises but also promotes sustained growth and sustainable development. JSON: Name: teapot_design_sem_repurchase Title: Structural equation modeling of the effect of teapot design features on consumer repurchase intention in the Chinese tea-set market Short Hypothesis: Increased teapot design novelty (shape and pattern) causes higher consumer affective reactions, which increase customer satisfaction and thereby raise repurchase intention. Related Work: Existing work on repurchase intention has followed two main strands: (1) behavioral and satisfaction-based models that link satisfaction, perceived value, price and service quality to repurchase intention using regression or structural equation modeling; and (2) product-design and aesthetics studies that measure how visual novelty, pattern, and form influence emotional and cognitive responses. Prior analyses commonly model cognition and affect as separate predictors or treat design as an exogenous attribute. Methodologically, most studies rely on cross-sectional surveys and confirmatory SEM, while a minority apply predictive machine-learning classifiers to forecast purchase likelihood. Limitations in prior work include domain-general samples (few studies dedicated to culturally specific product categories like tea sets), limited integration of both cognitive and affective mediators in a single model, inconsistent treatment of brand credibility as moderator (often underpowered to detect interaction effects), heavy reliance on self-report without behavioral validation, and sparse comparison to alternative predictive baselines or ablation studies that isolate the contribution of design, display, price and service quality. Abstract: This study investigates whether teapot design novelty (shape and pattern) drives repurchase intention by increasing affective reactions and customer satisfaction. We propose and test a mediated structural equation model that places design features as antecedents of affective response, with cognitive reactions, price perception, physical evidence, and service quality included as cognitive antecedents, and brand credibility as a moderator. The main contribution is an integrated measurement and structural model that quantifies direct and indirect paths from design to repurchase intention and evaluates the moderating role of brand credibility. We estimate the model using consumer survey data and report measurement model validity, path coefficients, explained variance, and bootstrapped mediation effects. Expected outcomes are a quantified contribution of design-driven affect to satisfaction and repurchase, empirical evidence of mediation by affect, and assessment of whether brand credibility amplifies affect→satisfaction effects. Results will inform design- and brand-centered strategies to increase repurchase in culturally-significant consumer goods. Experiments: Datasets: (1) Primary survey: n=600 consumers sampled across at least three Chinese regions (urban/rural strata) collected online and in-store; (2) Replication holdout: n=300 from different regions and platform; (3) Behavioral validation subset: n≈200 with recorded follow-up purchase behavior (30–90 day). Questionnaire: use multi-item Likert scales per constructs in Table 11 (price perception, physical evidence, service quality, modeling design, pattern design, cognitive reactions, affective reactions, customer satisfaction, brand credibility, repurchase intention). Preprocessing: remove responses with >20% missing, impute remaining with item mean, inspect response distributions and common-method bias (Harman’s single-factor). Measurement model: perform EFA then CFA, report Cronbach’s alpha, AVE, CR; drop items with loadings <0.50. Structural model estimation: maximum likelihood SEM with robust SE; report standardized path coefficients, p-values, 95% bootstrap CIs (5,000 draws) and model fit indices (CFI, TLI, RMSEA, SRMR). Mediation tests: bootstrap indirect effects for design→affect→satisfaction→repurchase. Moderation tests: (a) create interaction terms affect×brand_cred and satisfaction×brand_cred (mean-centered) and test significance in SEM; (b) multi-group SEM split by high/low brand credibility to test path invariance. Baselines: (A) direct-effect SEM (design→repurchase no mediators), (B) cognitive-only SEM (exclude affective mediator), (C) predictive logistic regression and random forest trained to classify high vs low repurchase intention using same predictors, (D) SEM with tangible-display omitted. Ablation study: sequentially remove affective mediator, cognitive mediator, and physical evidence to quantify delta R^2 and changes in key path coefficients. Evaluation metrics: model fit (CFI≥0.90, TLI≥0.90, RMSEA≤0.06), standardized path betas and p-values, indirect effect significance (bootstrap CI not containing 0), R^2 for satisfaction and repurchase, AIC/BIC for model comparison, classification metrics for predictive baselines (AUC, accuracy, F1, precision, recall). Statistical power: ensure sample provides ≥10 observations per estimated parameter and conduct post-hoc power for key indirect effects. Replication: repeat full analysis on holdout dataset and report parameter agreement and differences (Δbeta, z-tests). Risk Factors and Limitations: Measurement bias and common-method variance from self-report survey; cross-sectional design limits causal inference despite mediation modeling; sample representativeness risks (regional, demographic skew, online vs offline differences); social desirability and recall biases in responses; low AVE or Cronbach’s alpha for some constructs (e.g., price perception) may impair construct validity; interaction effects (moderation by brand credibility) may be underpowered and produce false negatives; multicollinearity among predictors (price, service quality, physical evidence) can inflate SEs and destabilize path estimates; SEM identification issues if model over-parameterized relative to sample size; limited external validity to other product categories, cultures, or channels (online imagery vs physical display); behavioral purchase data may be unavailable or noisy, constraining validation of stated intentions; scalability of findings to large populations may be limited without broader sampling; reliance on Likert scales imposes ordinal measurement assumptions that can affect ML baselines and classification thresholds.
